TICKET DETAILS

Calculation notes

Verified Power BI criteria

All five original pages were inspected. The semantic model yielded 123 DAX measures, 88 calculated columns (including automatic date columns), 13 calculated tables and two Power Query definitions. Open to inspect every expression and visual query.

SA uses Service Impacted = Outage. NSA uses Service Impacted ≠ Outage, including Degraded and blank impacts, exactly as the saved report filters. Every page requires blank Parent TT; SA pages retain their own root cause exclusions. The “All recorded faults” scope removes parent and root cause exclusions within the page’s impact group.

Counts, durations and calendar

Ticket volume = COUNTROWS of the filtered fact table. Distinct ticket numbers are shown separately. The Power Query grain is Ticket Number + Severity + SiteID + District. The stored PBIX has one repeated grain key; both rows remain visible and flagged. New raw CSV imports retain the first row at that grain; prepared PBIX variant keys preserve the saved model rows.

New Duration Dax Min = RestorationTime HHMMSS × 1440. Total hours = sum of those minutes ÷ 60. Mean restoration uses records with a duration. Missing values and recorded zero remain distinct. Duration bands are <2hrs, 02–04hrs, 04–08hrs, 08–24hrs and ≥24hrs (the original label is “>24hrs”).

Dates use Create Date in Asia/Riyadh. Weeks use WEEKNUM(Date,1): Sunday starts, and January 1 belongs to week 1. Weekly overviews compare adjacent weeks. Monthly overview compares the selected review month to the previous months. MoM Y compares that month across years; WoW Y compares that week number across years. YoY compares matching year-to-date coverage through the selected review month. Partial months in MoM Y use matching days. Partial coverage is labelled.

Legacy formula findings

The saved model contains no calendar relationships. Some DAX measures hard-code August 1–30, mix week 12 ticket volume with week 22 duration, use the entire prior year at January/week 1, or subtract a fixed four tickets. Those exact formulas are preserved in the audit. Live dashboards explicitly filter Create Date, include full selected months, use adjacent periods at year boundaries, and show observed row counts without the unexplained −4. These changes make future uploads comparable.

Changes use (current − previous) ÷ previous × 100. New activity against zero displays +100%; both zero displays 0%, following the report’s weekly rule. Periods outside source coverage display no comparison. The original “Outperform SLA %” visual references ticket-change measures; it is not treated as an SLA percentage.

SLA and data refresh

Source SLA compliance = non-breached ÷ eligible records. Eligibility requires a recorded Yes/No in Exceed SLA and no explicit SLA exclusion. This is labelled separately from the legacy calculated SLA columns, which have no stored values in this file. Network availability is not calculated without a historical on-air inventory denominator.

A connected, approved Supabase account checks for a new completed cumulative snapshot every 30 seconds while this tab is visible. All six dashboards switch together after the row count is verified. Pending or failed uploads keep the previous complete snapshot live. The private Power BI baseline remains a static snapshot until you sign in to the database.
